title: Pairing offer
description: What the Hub's "add device" screen offers a new Device (D6): the QR code holds this JSON. It is good once, for five minutes. The manual code carries nothing else: the Hub shows the secret as eight groups of four lowercase hex digits joined by -, the user types hub_url, and the client drops spaces and - from what the user typed and lowercases it before it sends it as device/pair_request secret. It then takes hub_id from the CampusLife-Hub-Id of the pair response. Open.

hub_url.description: The Hub's origin as tailscale serve publishes it: https://<host> or https://<host>:<port>, with no path, a lowercase host as MagicDNS names are, and a port from 1 to 65535. A client sends every request to hub_url followed by the path, such as /v1/pair. The Hub leaves out :443, which the pattern still takes since it names the same origin; a client tells Hubs apart by hub_id, never by hub_url. maxLength 267 is https:// (8) plus a DNS name of at most 253 characters (RFC 1035) plus :65535 (6).

hub_id.description: The Hub the client pairs with and keeps checking against CampusLife-Hub-Id (D3).
